name: Syndromic Agammaglobulinemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Immunological Diagnostic Criteria for Syndromic Agammaglobulinemia

criteria.description: Marked reduction or absence of peripheral B lymphocytes
Severe reduction in serum immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, IgM)
History of recurrent severe bacterial infections, especially respiratory and gastrointestinal
Presence of associated syndromic features such as developmental delay, skeletal abnormalities, or facial dysmorphism
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with syndromic agammaglobulinemia (e.g., BTK, others)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent or markedly reduced B cells, severe hypogammaglobulinemia, and recurrent bacterial infections
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis and identify specific gene mutations.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked absence of peripheral B lymphocytes
Severe hypogammaglobulinemia (low IgG, IgA, IgM levels)
searchTerms: hypogammaglobulinemia with low IgG, IgA, IgM

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent severe bacterial infections (e.g., pneumonia, otitis media)
searchTerms: frequent serious bacterial infections like pneumonia
recurrent infections such as ear infections

common.symptomName: Facial dysmorphism (e.g., hypertelorism, flat nasal bridge)
searchTerms: unusual facial features like wide-set eyes
facial differences including flat nose bridge

common.symptomName: Chronic diarrhea due to gastrointestinal infections

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby

laboratory: Absent or markedly reduced CD19+ B cells in peripheral blood
Normal or elevated T cell counts
imaging: Chest X-ray showing recurrent pneumonia or bronchiectasis
Skeletal X-rays revealing joint abnormalities or scoliosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in BTK gene or other genes associated with syndromic agammaglobulinemia
other: Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance
Poor response to vaccines due to absent antibody production

distinguishingFeatures: BTK mutations without additional developmental abnormalities
Variable immunoglobulin levels with presence of B cells
Later onset and less severe B cell deficiency
Combined T and B cell deficiency
More severe infections including opportunistic pathogens

redFlags: Recurrent severe bacterial infections in infancy
Markedly reduced or absent B cells on immunophenotyping
Failure to thrive with associated syndromic features
references: Notarangelo LD. Primary immunodeficiencies. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2010;125(2 Suppl 2):S182-94.

Picard C, Al-Herz W, Bousfiha A, et al. Primary Immunodeficiency Diseases: An Update on the Classification from the International Union of Immunological Societies Expert Committee for Primary Immunodeficiency. Front Immunol. 2015;6:54.
